correctness.rationale: For every finite real A, every K>=1 and 1<=r<n, the white-noise covariance is exactly sigma^2 omega f_K(omega A^T A). The derivative equation proves a unique interior maximum of f_K for K>=2. Unimodality proves f_K(t)<=M_K f_K(s) whenever t<=s; for each worst omitted mode this forces r retained and one omitted covariance eigenvalues to be >= its weight/M_K. The resulting eigenvalue counting yields the all-rank spectral bound by the best-rank theorem. The (r+1)-dimensional spectrum with r unit eigenvalues and one critical eigenvalue attains equality. Uniform compactness yields the sharp M_K/K asymptotic. The K=1, zero-eigenvalue and zero-best-error boundaries are covered. Extracted checker passed 24486 finite assertions, supplementary only.

value.rationale: Low-rank normal-operator truncation is a motivated approximation used to accelerate propagated uncertainty evaluation. The natural rank-r operator-norm competitiveness loss against the best covariance rank-r approximation is determined exactly, uniformly over dimension and retained rank, with a sharp r+1 dimensional extremal family and a growth law approximately 0.407264 K. The result distinguishes singular-mode ranking for reconstruction from mode ranking for noise uncertainty. It does not claim improvements or degradation in coverage, bias, or randomized residual-corrected implementations.
